subject: Model slate + traffic estimate — Implementation handoff for SableHealth
messages:
From: Evan Marsh <evan.m@sablehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: SableHealth Technical Lead <techlead@sablehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial traffic snapshot & ask for model recommendations

Hi Jonas / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo today. Per our conversation, attaching a quick traffic snapshot so you can recommend an initial model slate and expected token spend. Key points:
- Live users: ~18k weekly active; peak concurrent sessions ~750 (weekdays 10-3 PT).
- Average prompt length: ~120 tokens; typical assistant response ~220 tokens.
- 90th percentile session includes 2 turns (user question + follow-up).

Can you send a candidate model list with context-length guidance (we expect user prompts may include a short transcript ~800 tokens for certain workflows) and a 6-week token spend estimate for our first phase? Security/compliance chat later but for now want cost/latency sizing.

Attachments: sable_traffic_estimates.csv

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Marsh
Head of Product, SableHealth
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Evan Marsh <evan.m@sablehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-08T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic snapshot & ask for model recommendations

Evan —

Thanks for the numbers, this is very helpful. I've attached a short spreadsheet with three candidate slates and an initial 6-week token estimate based on the profile you sent (see model_slate_summary.xlsx). High-level recommendations up front:

1) Baseline cost-efficient slate (Phase 1): RW-7B-instruct (q4/8 quantized) for most NLU; RW-Chat-13B for higher-quality threads where >600 token context is required.
2) Quality-first slate (canary): RW-Chat-30B-v1 for complex clinical summarization paths (expected lower throughput but much higher fidelity).
3) Fallback / low-latency variant: flan-t5-xl small-deploy for short prompts / routing under heavy load.

Context guidance: if you expect transcripts ~800 tokens as part of the prompt occasionally, recommend reserving the 13B model for those flows; RW-7B should be fine for <400 token contexts. For throughput we assumed 80% of requests will be handled by the 7B route, 15% by 13B, 5% by 30B in Phase 1.

Next asks from our side to tighten estimates:
- A sample of the 800-token transcript (we can redact PII) to validate tokenization patterns.
- Clarify SLA targets (p95 latency target).

I've cc'd Ben to start mapping capacity/estimated GPU-hours. Attaching eval prompt set to sanity-check output quality quickly.

Attachments: model_slate_summary.xlsx, eval_prompt_set.zip

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Evan Marsh <evan.m@sablehealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-09T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic snapshot & ask for model recommendations

Evan — quick follow-up with a digestible shortlist and concrete token math to slot into procurement/finance.

Shortlist rationale (separate doc: model_shortlist_notes.md attached):
- RW-7B-instruct-q4: Best cost-to-quality for intent extraction and short answer flows. Target context <= 400 tokens.
- RW-Chat-13B-v2: Good middle-ground; supports up to 2048 token contexts reliably in our tests. Use for transcript-included flows and clinical summarization.
- RW-Chat-30B-v1 (canary): reserve for heavy summarization where fidelity matters; expected 2-3x cost vs 13B.

6-week token estimate (Phase 1, conservative):
- Weekly active users: 18k -> estimated weekly requests: 90k (assuming 5 requests per active user/week)
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 360 tokens
- Weekly tokens: ~32.4M; 6 weeks: ~194.4M tokens
- Cost projection (ballpark using current hosted rates): $0.028/token-equivalent for mixed slate -> ~$5.4k/week -> ~$32.4k for 6 weeks (this is a high-level number; we'll refine once you confirm % routing).

Operational notes:
- Recommend enabling prefix caching for common prompts and a 10s hot-window to reduce repeat tokenization cost.
- Plan a 2-week canary (10% traffic) for the 13B model with QA prompts from your product team.

If you confirm routing percentages (7B/13B/30B split), Ben will produce a capacity plan (GPU-hours) and we will provide a canary runbook.

Attachments: model_shortlist_notes.md

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Marsh <evan.m@sablehealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: SableHealth Technical Lead <techlead@sablehealth.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic snapshot & ask for model recommendations

Thanks both — this is very actionable. A few clarifications so our procurement and infra teams can proceed:

1) We want the 13B model to handle any request with a transcript attached (>600 tokens). Routing split we propose: 75% 7B / 20% 13B / 5% 30B during the first 6 weeks.
2) Latency SLA: p95 user-facing latency target 400ms for the 7B path, 900ms p95 for 13B. Is that feasible with Redwood Dedicated, or will we need to accept higher p95?
3) Security: we'll start the SOC2 checklist in parallel; for now assume hosted API for Phase 1.

Also please include a simple canary checklist (what the product team should watch for in the first 48 hours) and proposed rollback criteria. We'll finalise routing after procurement signs the PO.

—Evan
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Evan Marsh <evan.m@sablehealth.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic snapshot & ask for model recommendations

Evan —

Appreciate the routing split and SLA targets. Quick summary and an implementation playbook attached (implementation_playbook.pdf) that your SREs and product QA can use. Highlights:

- Feasibility: With Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool, optimized batch sizing) we can hit ~350-420ms p95 for the 7B path and ~700-950ms p95 for the 13B path depending on chosen instance type and sequence-length distribution. Ben has sketched GPU-hour estimates in the attached.

- Canary checklist (48h):
  * Start with 10% traffic to 13B for transcript flows; monitor quality metrics (ROUGE/clinical summary spot-checks) and latency at route granularity.
  * Watch error rate (>=0.5% sustained) and CPU/GPU queue length. If error rate >1% or p95 exceeds SLA by >30% for 1h, rollback to 7B routing for affected endpoint.
  * Compare sampled outputs against eval_prompt_set reference set; flag regressions where automated scoring drops >8 points.

- Rollback criteria: sustained latency > SLA + 30% for 1h OR error rate >1% for 30m OR a quality regression >8 pts on the reference set.

Next steps (action items):
1) Evan — sign off on the PO routing split and confirm whether you want Hosted->Dedicated migration at week 4.
2) Ben — produce GPU-hour commitment table for the 6-week window (attached in playbook).
3) Monica / Jonas — schedule a 60-min runbook walkthrough with your SREs and product QA next week.

Links: HubSpot deal and onboarding Drive folder are in the metadata. We'll drop a short Marcom blurb for the CSM once onboarding starts.

Thanks — attaching the playbook and the final traffic spreadsheet for procurement.

Attachments: implementation_playbook.pdf, sable_traffic_estimates.csv

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
